senses.definition: On the whole, allowing for exceptions you are not going to list. It concedes counterexamples exist while saying they do not change the conclusion.
senses.caution: It signals you have not checked the exceptions. Safe in conversation, risky in writing that will be scrutinised, because this is exactly where someone asks which cases you are excluding.
senses.example: By and large the migration went clean. Two services needed manual work.

cues.text: Your sponsor asks how the rollout went. It went well, and there were two ugly cases you would rather not itemise right now.
You are summarising six months of model performance to a board and do not want to caveat every quarter.
Someone asks how your holiday was. Good, apart from one bad day you do not want to dwell on.
A friend asks whether you liked a novel. You did, with reservations you are not going to list over dinner.
A colleague asks whether the new review process is working. It is, for most teams, and you do not want to claim it is universal.

distractors: In every single case without exception, which is a much stronger claim than it sounds.
At a level of description kept deliberately free of detail, so the shape of a thing is visible and its mechanics are not.
According to the view most of the people in the room hold, offered as the reason a decision should go that way. It reports a headcount rather than a judgement.
Measured across a stretch of time long enough that short-term noise stops mattering, which is how a trend gets separated from a run of bad weeks. It is a claim about duration, not about coverage.

Taken across every part of an organisation rather than inside one team, which is what makes a number comparable between divisions. It widens the frame of a claim from local to enterprise-wide, and it usually raises the stakes of it.
